fact: The brightest star in Earth's night sky — and one of our nearest stellar neighbours at 8.6 light-years.
bio: Sirius (Alpha Canis Majoris) is a hot, blue-white main-sequence star with a faint white-dwarf companion, Sirius B, the burnt-out core of a once more-massive star. Its brilliance comes from a genuinely luminous star sitting unusually close to us.
cultural: The 'Dog Star' has guided calendars for millennia: its heliacal rising once heralded the annual flooding of the Nile in ancient Egypt, and it anchors the 'Dog Days' of summer in the Greco-Roman tradition.
